name: Is building an ADU in Los Angeles still worth it in 2026, and what kind of rental income can I realistically expect?

mainEntity.name: Is building an ADU in Los Angeles still worth it in 2026, and what kind of rental income can I realistically expect?

acceptedAnswer.text:
For many homeowners, building an ADU in Los Angeles is still financially attractive in 2026, especially in high-demand rental areas, but the numbers depend on your total project cost, financing, and local rents. Many well-located ADUs can generate meaningful monthly cash flow or offset a mortgage. 
Context: ADU-friendly state laws have made permitting easier, but construction costs have also risen, so feasibility comes down to balancing build cost against realistic rent and upkeep. ADUs can also add resale appeal and provide housing for family members. 
Key factors:
- All-in ADU cost (design, permits, utilities, construction, landscaping)
- Long-term vs short-term rental strategy and local rules
- Neighborhood market rents for comparable studios/1-bed units
- Financing costs and property tax implications
Practical guidance: Get a ballpark ADU cost from a contractor and compare it to conservative rent estimates from a local agent or property manager. Run a simple cash-flow analysis that includes vacancy, maintenance, and loan payments before committing. Soft positioning: A contractor with ADU experience can help you create a scope that aligns with your financial targets and intended use.
acceptedAnswer.description: In many parts of Los Angeles, ADUs still pencil out in 2026, but it depends on your total build cost and neighborhood rents. Estimate your all-in project cost, get conservative rent numbers from local comps, and run cash-flow scenarios—including financing and maintenance—before deciding to move forward.
